messages:
maria_cs: Hey team — Azimuth reported intermittent 429s and big tail latency during their marketing blast last night. They're on a Dedicated pool (azimuth-east-1). They say baseline QPS ~600, peak bursts to ~2.1k for ~7-10m windows. They also saw repeated client retries which ballooned token use and billing. Logs attached.
lee_sre: @maria_cs can you paste the pool config, autoscale policy, and the model they were serving? Also any client repro commands they ran.
maria_cs: Pool: azimuth-east-1-reserved, nodes: 4 (RTX-like), reserved_qps: 1200, autoscale: enabled, scale_up at 75% util, max_nodes: 8. Model: gpt-neox-20b-8bit-qat. Client used a fan-out campaign hitting multiple endpoints; they also used a retry backoff of 200ms.
jonathan_eng: That config looks tight for 2.1k bursts. If baseline is 600 and they only reserved 1200, autoscale needs to react under 7-10m bursts. What's the autoscale cooldown and ramp? Could be slow ramp causing 429s.
olivia_platform: autoscale cooldown is 300s (5m) on that pool, scale step +1 node. With bursts of 7-10m and step +1 every 5m we can be underprovisioned for the first 1-2 steps. Also gpt-neox-20b 8-bit on current kernel has higher latency per token than some quantized variants — throughput per GPU may be lower than expected.
lee_sre: Can we repro quickly? If yes, request Azimuth to run a controlled test (or we run from our infra). A reproducible load pattern helps decide: is it autoscale latency, noisy neighbor, or model throughput saturation.
maria_cs: They shared a reproducer command they used (vegeta):

```
echo "GET https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" > targets.txt
vegeta attack -targets=targets.txt -rate=2100 -duration=8m -connections=500 | vegeta report
```

They also included 429 snippets:

```
{"error":"ThrottleError","message":"dedicated pool capacity exceeded","code":429}
```

and p99 latency jumps to 2.1s before errors.
jonathan_eng: Good. Probable causes in order: 1) autoscale step/count too small + long cooldown 2) insufficient per-node throughput for that model variant 3) noisy neighbor on one node causing tail latency. We should check per-instance GPU_util, mem, and per-instance p95/p99 routing stats.
lee_sre: I'll pull instance metrics for azimuth-east-1-reserved for the window 2026-12-01T22:00Z to 22:20Z and check per-node GPU util + tail latencies. If one node shows 100% util while others idle that points at noisy neighbor or imbalance.
sre-bot: Scheduled: metrics query job queued (job id: metrics-azimuth-185246). ETA 2m.
maria_cs: Also flagged: customer reported tokenization auth errors earlier in the night (401) but that looks separate — possibly a transient key rotation. They said billing got higher due to retries — we should summarize for CS later.
jonathan_eng: Quick mitigation suggestions to propose to customer now: 1) increase reserved nodes from 4->6 temporarily (adds headroom) 2) lower autoscale cooldown to 60s and increase scale step to +2 nodes 3) enable burst capacity (if enabled in their plan) 4) consider switching to a faster quantized model or reduce max sequence length in campaign.
olivia_platform: I can push a config change to lower cooldown and bump max_nodes to 12 in the control plane for a short window if CS approves. That requires a short outage for a rolling config update (~1-2m of control plane ops only).
lee_sre: I'll try a rolling restart on node-3 in that pool (suspect noisy neighbor) during a quieter minute — will coordinate with CS. If restart reduces p99 we confirm noisy neighbor.
maria_cs: Customer ok with temporary increases and a restart. Please keep them in loop: azimuth_prod@customer (they want updates). :thumbsup:
jonathan_eng: After we stabilize, we should run a capacity plan: derive throughput per node for the actual workload (seq len distribution, temperature, top_k), compute nodes_needed = ceil(peak_qps / per_node_qps * safety_factor). Propose utilization target 55-65% for peak with 20% headroom for spikes.
maria_cs: Noted. I'll collect their seq length distribution and retry patterns and post here.
lee_sre: Follow-ups: pulling metrics now, will post a short summary and propose node bump timeline.
maria_cs: Thanks — will ping when I have the customer's repro artifacts and sequence histograms. :eyes:
